newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines likely to lower petrol, diesel prices.
newsitem.headline: Philippines likely to lower petrol, diesel prices.

text.p: The Philippines Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) is likely to lower the prices of petrol and diesel on Friday, ERB chairman Bayani Faylona told Reuters.
Prices of fuel oil will fall by about 20 centavos per litre, he said.
It will be the fifth time that goverment will adjust petroleum prices since an automatic oil price formula was adopted in August as part of the partial deregulation of the oil industry.

"We will announce the next round of adjustments tomorrow (Friday). Gasoline prices will either go down by a few centavos or remain the same," Faylona said. He added that diesel prices may drop by 10 centavos per litre.

Prices of other petroleum products will be raised. Faylona said that price of liquefied petroleum gas will be raised by an estimated 20 centavos per litre. Jet fuel and kerosene prices will also be raised although the amount has yet to be determined.

Under the deregulation law, the government adjusts petroleum product prices on or before the third Monday of every month using an automatic formula. The formula uses Singapore Posted Prices as a benchmark.
Petroleum product prices were raised last week by an average of 79.75 centavos per litre as the monthly adjustment for November was delayed due to opposition from some politicians.
